description: Tuning parameters for health evaluation, anomaly detection, trend prediction and diagnosis. Every value here is a TEAM ESTIMATE to be tuned against generated scenarios. The detector's physical models below are its own 'datasheet' beliefs; they start equal to config/generator.json but are deliberately kept separate so the detector never reads the generator's truth.

evaluation.notes: Evaluate once per 60 s batch. Judge a rolling-median-smoothed value, not single raw samples. Skip per_mode relative checks for 30 s after a mode change (current spikes while the robot starts or stops). Hard limits are never skipped. driving_modes: wheel channels are only trended and diagnosed on samples taken while driving (when parked, a wheel says nothing about its health).

anomaly.notes: Raise an anomaly only after 5 consecutive smoothed samples are past a limit (debounce against noise). Consider it cleared after 30 consecutive normal samples. Do not raise the same robot+channel+severity again within 600 s. Main defence against false positives that waste P5 capacity.

trend.notes: Fit the last 30 min of the deviation-from-baseline signal. Only extrapolate when the fit explains enough of the variation (R^2 >= 0.3) and the slope is at least 3 standard errors from zero. R^2 is set low because wheel current is noisy (terrain): a real wheel_drag trend over 30 min explains only about 35-40% of the variance. Trends are only fitted for robots the diagnosis has already flagged, so this cannot create false alarms on healthy robots. Report time-to-failure as the time the trend crosses the CRITICAL limit, with an 80% interval. Ignore predicted crossings more than 4 h away.

predictive_warning.notes: Issue a predictive warning when predicted time-to-failure is under 60 min with confidence >= 0.6. HUNCH's excellence example is 15 min (900 s) of lead time; we tune toward more. A new prediction for the same robot is only re-announced if the fault, severity or warning state changes, or the predicted failure time moves by more than republish_change_fraction of the time left (and at least republish_min_change_s). Losing the trend (e.g. after a stop) is not re-announced; the last prediction stands.

thermal_model.notes: Used for (1) the lagged thermal baseline and (2) the thermal residual: predicted T from measured current and speed, P = I^2 R + tau_b * omega, first-order lag to sink + P * R_th.

battery_model.notes: Baseline for battery_voltage_v = V_oc(SOC) - I * r_int_nominal. Linear interpolation in the table.

diagnosis.notes: Thresholds for turning each signature element (UP / DOWN / NORMAL / EXPLAINED_BY_CURRENT in config/faults.json) into a yes/no observation over the last 30 min. The diagnosis scores each of the four faults by how many signature elements match. Below min_confidence (or on a tie) the fault mode is reported as 'unknown'. temp_rise_c: a temperature that rose at least this much but has no unexplained heat counts as EXPLAINED_BY_CURRENT. Diagnosis only starts once some channel's recent median deviation reaches localise_min_fraction of its WARNING offset. recent_samples: how many of the latest relevant samples a shift or residual is measured over. normal_band_fraction: evidence only counts as NORMAL when it is within this fraction of its threshold; between that and the threshold it is UNCLEAR and matches no fault, so borderline evidence gives 'unknown' instead of a confident wrong answer. current_rise_a (0.3 A) and speed_drop_rads (-0.02 rad/s) are about 6 and 5 standard deviations of the healthy 300-sample median.

severity_rules.notes: Severity is WARNING or CRITICAL. CRITICAL if predicted time-to-failure < 30 min or any evidence channel is already CRITICAL.

health_score.notes: Robot health_score (0-100) = minimum of subsystem scores; subsystem score = points for its worst channel status. Placeholder rule - refine after PDR.
